newsitem.title: USA: Three women in army scandal are transferred.
newsitem.headline: Three women in army scandal are transferred.

text.p: Three women soldiers who said Army investigators pressured them to accuse superiors falsely of rape have received transfers to leave the base, a spokesman said Thursday.

The spokesman said the transfers from the Aberdeen Proving Ground were cleared last week and issued Monday and had no connection to Tuesday's news conference at which the three trainees and two other female soldiers aired their charges.

"I know it sounds coincidental but it was just the way it worked," said Ed Starnes, a spokesman for the Army Ordnance Centre and School. He said Pvt. Darla Hornberger, 30, had received a "compassionate assignment" transfer she had requested and would be sent to Fort Riley, Kansas.

Pvt. Brandi Krewson, 24, was ordered transfered to Fort Bragg, North Carolina, and Pvt. Kelly Wagner, 20, received a transfer to Fort Lewis, Washington. The locations of those transfers were "based on the needs of the Army," Starnes said.

He said the transfers following training at the school had been held up by the needs of the continuing investigation into sexual harassment at the base. Some of the women said Tuesday that transfers promised in the course of the investigation had never come through.

Of the other two women who made charges Tuesday, Pvt. Toni Moreland faces a court martial for recanting allegations of sexual misconduct and Kathryn Leming has left the military at the end of her regular term of service, Starnes said.
Hornberger declined to comment when asked her reaction to the transfer. The other two women could not be reached.

Attorney Stuart Robinson, who has worked with the women and the NAACP in questioning the conduct of the Army's investigation, said it was positive if the women's protests had helped speed the transfers.
"If their stepping up has helped the military expedite their assignments, then that's good. But this whole thing shouldn't have had to go to this extreme," Robinson said.
